evidence: Cic. Off. 2.31: sī est simpliciter breviterque dīcendum
Cael. in Cic. Fam. 8.6.1: simpliciter et candidē
terms.comment: Without art or ornament, or without holding anything back (Lewis & Short: “simply, plainly, straightforwardly … frankly, candidly”).

terms.gloss: plainly, clearly, so as to be understood
evidence: Cic. Phil. 7.17: quī plānē et Latīnē loquuntur
Cic. de Or. 2.303: ut plānius dīcam
terms.comment: “To put it more simply” is ut plānius dīcam. For “simply” meaning “absolutely” (simply impossible), see quite.

terms.gloss: speak plainly, say it in plain words
evidence: Cic. Phil. 7.17: quī plānē et Latīnē loquuntur
Traupman p. 110: Latīnē loquī cum (+ ablative)
terms.comment: Plain Latin is plain speech: sī Latīnē loquī volumus, if we are to use words properly (Cic. Caecin. 21, Lewis & Short s.v. armō).

phrases.latin: Haec autem, sī est simpliciter breviterque dīcendum, quibus rēbus pariuntur ā singulīs, eīsdem ferē ā multitūdine.
phrases.english: To put it simply and briefly, these are won from the many by much the same means as from one person.

phrases.latin: solēre mē cēdere et, ut plānius dīcam, fugere
phrases.english: that I usually give ground, or, to put it more plainly, run away

sources: Lewis & Short: simplex (simpliciter) · Lewis & Short: planus (plānē)
